p.i: libus humi gradientibus, sequuntur reptilia, ut serpens, vipera, omnisq; generis vermes & insecta, ut formica, scorpius, aranei, cimices, pediculi, pinorum truca[?] : nec non pennata quaedam, ut musca, papiliones, apes, vespae, scarabaei.

main_text.head: CAP. XV. De serpentina & viperina.
main_text.p: Est[?] ophiophagos, serpentibus vesci af-suetos, Caudeos vocatos, à grauissimis auctoribus proditum reperitur. Solin. c.36[?]. Plin.l.6.c.29. Et fuisse in Africa Marsos, & Psyllos, nec non Ophiogenes in Cypro, quorum illis exitiale virus serpentibus inge-Miratu digna.nitum erat, vt odore solo eas sopirent, his ve-rò[?] serpentum ictus solo cotaculeuare[?], manuque impolita venenum corpori extrahere, huiusque experimenti causa ex Ophiogenarum familia legatus Exagon nomine, à Consulibus Romae in dolium serpentum coniectus circummulcentibus[?] linguis miraculum praebuit : Signumque eius familiae est, si adhuc durat, vernis temporibus odoris virus. Plin.l.28.c.3. Qui Athon montem incolunt viperinis carnibus vescuntur, itaq; nec capiti nec vestibus eorum noxia corpori innasci animalia, certi autores tradunt. page.notes: The first word of the text is an initial E joined to "Sfe", read as "Est" with a doubtful letter. The italic opening line begins mid-word ("libus"), a fragment carried over from the previous page. "truca" is doubtful. "rò" and "cotaculeuare" are doubtful readings. "circummulcentibus" is doubtful. The marginal note "Miratu / digna." is set as one note beside the lines "inge-" and "ve-". The catchword "nam" follows the text ending "viperi-".
